observations: Two large black squares sit side by side in the upper half, each topped with a row of red looping lines and containing a spiral form—the left one coiled white with a blue center, the right one blue with radiating spokes.

A wide black band across the lower third holds a row of white rectangular shapes, flanked on both sides by smaller white-and-red bead-like forms strung along horizontal lines that extend beyond the central mass.
Loose yellow, red, and white lines scatter across the olive-brown background, forming open loops, brackets, and short dashes that do not close into solid shapes.
reading: Two paired black squares anchor the upper half, each holding a spiral—one coiled and white, one splayed and blue. Below, a wide dark band opens into a row of white rectangles that reads as a gaping mouth. Bead strings extend outward along horizontal lines, blurring where the central form ends. The scattered lines on the olive ground feel restless, as if the face has not fully settled at its edges.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, title neighbors #118 and #120 share the wide tooth-band and paired upper zones. #119 replaces #118's blue-grey ground and pink outlines with an olive field and red-yellow palette, giving the same structural idea a heavier, more grounded feel.

connections.reason: Both works use a wide lower band of white tooth shapes with flanking bead strings, but #118 sets this against a blue-grey ground with pink outlines while #119 uses olive and red-yellow, making the structural parallel and color contrast directly visible.

#120 shares the tooth-row band and paired upper zones, but its teal ground and dense pink-red crosshatching produce a busier surface compared to #119's more open olive field and isolated scatter lines.

lookingQuestion: The bead-like forms strung along horizontal lines appear both inside the central mass and out on the background—where exactly does the boundary of the face begin and end?
ambiguities: nnotb #204 shares an olive ground and layered line density but its structural organization differs enough that no strong formal connection was identified; it was not selected.
Title-derived order and recorded-creation order align for this work in the owned subset, but gaps exist in the full catalogue so no sequence claims are made.
